itens.titulo: Marvell Just Bet $115 Billion On AI's 'Once In A Generation' Opportunity. Should You Buy The Stock?
itens.descricao: Marvell Just Bet $115 Billion On AI's 'Once In A Generation' Opportunity. Should You Buy The Stock? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Marvell (NASDAQ:MRVL) stock fell 13% on Thursday when word of a Lumentum (NASDAQ:LITE) takeover leaked, and the official terms, announced Monday, show what holders are paying.

Marvell, which designs chips for data infrastructure, agreed to buy the optical-parts maker for about $115 billion in an all-stock deal, handing Lumentum's owners about a third of the combined company.

What Marvell Holders Give Up Lumentum shareholders will receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each Lumentum share, or about $1,132 a share, a premium of about 23.9% to the October 28 closing prices, the last trading day before deal speculation began.
After closing, current Marvell holders will own about 67% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis, and Lumentum holders about 33%.
In the meantime, the deal is not expected to close until the first half of 2028, and it needs approval from both companies' shareholders and from regulators.
In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia.
For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia.
Its latest quarter, which ended on September 26, brought revenue up 136.5% to $1.26 billion, and it guided to roughly $350 million more next quarter, according to the Monday release.

itens.titulo: INTC Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and PC Weakness
itens.descricao: INTC Q3 Earnings Call Highlights AI Demand and PC Weakness Yahoo Finance
trechos: Intel Corporation INTC highlighted surging server processor demand during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, while warning that memory shortages and weakening PC demand will pressure near-term performance.
Intel reported adjusted earnings of $0.52 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.39.
Revenues of $16.51 billion surpassed the consensus estimate of $16.44 billion.
Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenues increased 78% year over year to $7.3 billion.
Tan estimated that the server CPU market could expand from $40 billion to more than $200 billion over five years, driven largely by agentic workloads.
Client Computing and Physical AI Group revenues declined 5% year over year to $8.1 billion.
Management expects industry PC unit shipments to fall approximately 12% in 2026 and roughly 10% in 2027.
Zinsner clarified that inventory adjustments could extend into the second quarter of 2027, while memory-related market weakness is expected to persist throughout the year.

itens.titulo: MicroStrategy and Strive Buy More Bitcoin, but Shareholders Could Feel the Pain
itens.descricao: MicroStrategy and Strive Buy More Bitcoin, but Shareholders Could Feel the Pain Yahoo Finance
trechos: Both companies announced new purchases on Monday, November 2.
- Strategy bought 811 BTC for $65.5 million, bringing its total holdings to 849,327 BTC.
- Strive added another 124 BTC, taking its holdings to 43,124 BTC.
Why MicroStrategy Shareholders Could Lose Out Strategy sold approximately 1.18 million new MSTR shares to raise $164 million.
It used just $65.5 million to buy Bitcoin and kept the remainder as cash.
As a result, the Bitcoin represented by each diluted MSTR share fell approximately 0.17%.
Meanwhile, Strategy spent $208 million buying back its STRC preferred stock, more than three times its Bitcoin spending.

Strategy CEO Phong Le previously described the effort as a commitment to "returning STRC to health." Strive's Bitcoin Purchase Tells a Different Story Strive's latest filing shows its diluted share count remained unchanged while its Bitcoin holdings increased.
